newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia Bank approves SKB London listing.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia Bank approves SKB London listing.

text.p: Slovenia's second largest bank SKB said on Wednesday it had gained approval from the Bank of Slovenia to list its shares on the London bourse.
It said the central bank agreed late on Tuesday to increase the maximum holding by foreigners to 49 percent from the current 30 percent.
"This enables us to list our shares abroad but it is too early yet to say when that will happen," Barbara Grenko, SKB's consultant to international banking director, told Reuters.

SKB, which hopes to be listed on the London stock exchange in the first half of this year, has already approached Nomura International and the Bank of New York to act as advisors in its bid for a listing.

Shares of SKB, which are listed on the main market of the Ljubljana bourse, have not been traded since Monday when their average price rose by over 30 percent since the bank's last published announcement on the price of its shares, issued on October 7 last year.

According to Slovenian regulations, trading in a stock is suspended whenever the share price rises or falls by 30 percent from the company's last public announcement. The company must then issue a statement within 5 days to explain the share price movement. Trading resumes a day later.
SKB said it would issue a new announcement by Friday. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana Newsroom, 386-61-126-3644
